sections.body: When a piece attacks the enemy king, the king is in CHECK. A player in check must get out of it at once. There are three ways: move the king to a safe square, block the attack with another piece, or capture the piece that is giving check.
If the king is in check and none of those three ways works, it is CHECKMATE. The game is over and the player who gave checkmate wins.

STALEMATE is different. It happens when the player to move is NOT in check but has no legal move at all. A stalemate is a draw, not a win. Beware of it when you are winning: if you take away every square from the lone enemy king without giving check, you may draw by accident.
A back-rank checkmate is a common one: a king stuck on its first row behind its own pawns is attacked by a rook along that row, and has nowhere to go.
Set up a white king, a white queen and a black king. Can you checkmate? Then move the queen so that the black king has no move but is not in check. What happened?

Stalemate surprises many beginners. Practise with a king and queen against a lone king: try to give checkmate without stalemating. The chess puzzles in the app have only checkmates and winning tactics, so they never end in a stalemate.

quiz.q: Black's king is in check from a white queen, but the king can safely capture the queen. Is it checkmate?
options: No, the king can escape by capturing
Yes, any check is always checkmate
Yes, because a queen is a very strong piece
hints: Checkmate means the king has NO way out.
Capturing the piece that gives check is one of the three ways out of check.
Example: a king in check that can step to a safe square is not mated. Decide if capturing the queen is a way out here.
quiz.explain: Capturing the checking piece is one of the three ways to answer check. If it is safe to do, it is not checkmate.

quiz.q: It is Black's move. Black's king on h8 is not in check, but every square it could go to is attacked, and Black has no other pieces. What is the result?
hints: No. The king has no legal move, but it is not attacked.
Example: a player in check with no escape is checkmated. A player NOT in check with no legal move is something else. Decide which case this is.
quiz.explain: The player to move has no legal move and is not in check. That is stalemate, which is a draw.

quiz.q: A white rook gives check along the back row to a king hidden behind its own three pawns, and nothing can block or capture it. What is this called?
options: A stalemate on the back row
A fork with the rook and king
hints: Look at where the king is and what traps it.
The king's own pawns stop it from stepping forward, so the check along the back row cannot be escaped.
Example: a king surrounded by its own pieces cannot move to those squares. Name the mate that happens on the back row.
quiz.explain: The king is trapped on its back row by its own pawns, and the rook attacks along that row. This is a back-rank mate.
